mechanism_narrative: A positive GROCERY_PHARM trend signals normalization of essential errands and releases pent-up local spending. As grocery and pharmacy visits stay positive, adjacent retail-and-recreation footfall rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 0.0 at t-3w to 8.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above +5 for four weeks and the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to -27.15, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS crossing above the -35 percent baseline indicates outdoor recreation normalization. This raises discretionary mobility and pulls RETAIL_REC up over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -41.4 at t-2w to -33.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS rises above -35% baseline and the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than or equal to -27.15, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Coincident positive GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT recovery above -20 means errand-based trips are resuming. The interaction amplifies retail-and-recreation visits, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM > 0 and TRANSIT > -20 both hold for two weeks but the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to -27.15, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In an elevated-residential regime above 8 percent, home-centered activity supports neighborhood retail. Stable high residential mobility keeps local demand elevated, pushing RETAIL_REC up over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 8.3 and 9.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 8 percent and RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days falls below -24.1, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES falling below -28 percent signals renewed remote-work retreat, reducing weekday commuter spending. This drags RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -24.4 at t-1w to -28.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains below -28 percent and the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is greater than -27.15, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week TRANSIT decline signals a temporary mobility pullback. Retail-and-recreation visits follow transit down over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 1 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined from -17.6 at t-1w to -19.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls more than 1 point week-on-week but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is above -24.1, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Late-August back-to-school demand lifts GROCERY_PHARM and spills into retail-and-recreation as families shop. Seasonal spending keeps RETAIL_REC above its recent four-week mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-08-15 falls in late-August back-to-school period
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains positive through August but the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to -27.15, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Easing restrictions are visible through joint recovery in PARKS and TRANSIT. When both improve together, policy-driven reopening unlocks retail-and-recreation capacity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves >5 points and TRANSIT improves >3 points over two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -41.4 to -33.1 and TRANSIT rose from -22.4 to -19.0 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: If joint PARKS and TRANSIT improvement occurs but the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to -27.15, the hypothesis is rejected.
